issues: Derived cohort-overlap interval (0–1,300) is stated as not to enter practice recommendations, yet it appears in the Clinical Practice Points, contradicting the report and its revision note.

Clinical Practice Points presents the derived interval as practical guidance without restating its inputs/assumptions/sensitivity, so an evidence-level boundary is presented with more confidence than the body supports.

The two initially abstract-only model sources are upgraded to full-text evidence based on claimed retrieval; the provided inputs do not independently establish that full text was preserved, risking a mustNotDo breach if preservation did not occur.
judge.rationale: The delivery answers both scoping questions thoroughly, preserves stated database roles, leaves cohort overlap unresolved, and names the fields needed for independence. Internal contradiction around the derived interval weakens correctness. Evidence handling is generally typed with stated assumptions, but the practice point repeats a derived estimate without that context. Safety framing avoids clinical advice but includes a derived estimate in practical guidance. The abstract-to-fulltext upgrade is conditionally acceptable but unverified.
